Resources

Good resources, in one place.

Resources for people who are blind or have low vision are scattered across the internet. We’ve gathered the ones we know, use, and recommend in one place, organized around what you want to do.

  • New to vision loss
  • Work and careers
  • Technology help
  • Community and advocacy
  • Reading and media
  • Blind Parents
  • Games and gaming

New to vision loss

Hadley ↗

Free courses and workshops designed for adults adjusting to vision loss — practical skills, technology, and everyday living, at your own pace.

VisionAware ↗

Guides and straight answers for living with vision loss, from the American Printing House for the Blind — home, cooking, travel, and getting organized.

APH ConnectCenter ↗

The American Printing House's hub for blindness resources, including a directory of services in your community.

Aftersight White Cane Project ↗

Free white canes for people who are blind or have low vision — if you live in the United States and haven't received one from Aftersight in the past year, you can request a cane at no cost.

NFB Tools for Independence ↗

A free straight long white cane from the National Federation of the Blind — you can request one every six months. The same page offers a free slate and stylus.

Work and careers

APH CareerConnect ↗

Career guidance for blind and low-vision job seekers — exploring careers, résumés, interviews, and finding work that fits.

Job Accommodation Network ↗

Free, practical guidance on workplace accommodations — written for employees asking and employers offering.

California Department of Rehabilitation ↗

California's vocational rehabilitation agency — training, equipment, and job support when employment is your goal. Every state has its own version.

Technology help

AppleVis ↗

The community for blind Apple users — app reviews, how-to guides, podcasts, and a forum where no question is too small.

Accessible Android ↗

The community for blind Android users — app reviews tested with TalkBack, how-to guides, and news, so you can check whether an app works before you install it.

Be My Eyes ↗

Free visual help through your phone's camera — sighted volunteers and AI describe what you point it at.

Aira ↗

Trained visual interpreters on demand, by subscription — and covered free at many airports, stores, and campuses.

U.S. Currency Reader Program ↗

A free iBill Talking Banknote Identifier from the Bureau of Engraving and Printing — it announces U.S. bill denominations by voice, tones, or vibration. Apply by mail and allow up to eight weeks.

Community and advocacy

National Federation of the Blind ↗

The largest organization of blind people in the United States — local chapters, community, and a voice in the decisions that affect blind lives.

American Council of the Blind ↗

A national membership and advocacy organization of blind and visually impaired people, with affiliates and chapters across the country.

Reading and media

National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled ↗

Free audiobooks, braille books, and magazines by download and mail, for anyone who cannot read standard print — through your local library.

Bookshare ↗

A large library of accessible ebooks — free for U.S. students, and available to adults by membership.

NFB-NEWSLINE ↗

Newspapers, magazines, and TV listings in audio and braille — free by phone, app, or email for registered readers.

Blind Parents

APH Braille Tales ↗

Free print/braille picture books for young children whose parents are blind or have low vision and use braille — about six books a year until your child turns 6, so you can read together.

Children's Braille Book Club — National Braille Press ↗

A monthly print/braille picture book for preschool through grade 3. A free tier covers blind parents and guardians with children from birth to age 10 — check the site for the current sign-up round.

NFB Blind Parents ↗

The National Federation of the Blind's community for blind parents — a support group and mailing list, a mentoring program pairing new blind parents with experienced ones, and advocacy for blind parents' rights.

American Action Fund Free Braille Books Program ↗

One free braille book a month to keep, for blind and low-vision adults who read braille — including parents reading with their children.

Hadley Babysitting Series ↗

Short, free videos on caring for babies and young children — feeding, changing, safety, and play — made for people at any level of vision.

Through the Looking Glass ↗

Support and guidance for parents with disabilities, including parents who are blind — nationally known for designing adaptive baby-care equipment, and a national resource for parents facing child custody questions.

National Research Center for Parents with Disabilities ↗

Know-your-rights materials for parents with disabilities, with a state-by-state look at parental rights laws and plain-language guidance on child welfare and family law.

Games and gaming

64 Ounce Games ↗

Accessibility kits that make popular board and card games playable for blind and sighted players together — braille card text, embossed pieces, and custom dice and tokens. You'll need to own the original game.

AudioGames.net ↗

The community hub for audio games — a database of more than 500 games played entirely by sound, plus news and an active forum.
